_comment: Stage-3 kinematics for gripper.xml. base = world-fixed root. All bodies stay at pos 0 0 0 (meshes carry world coords), so joints at q=0 reproduce the rest pose. Ranges are PLACEHOLDERS to visualize motion; refine from CAD. Axes in world frame (chain is identity-oriented). slide ranges in meters. Actuator gains tuned for stable, visible motion, not fidelity.
_ranges_note: Ranges set 2026-05-28 from the user's interactive testing in the MuJoCo viewer (supersede earlier collision/placeholder values). Per-DOF ranges are in the joints block above (up pair != down pair, per user tuning); q=0 = CAD rest pose. Sign: +q on a rack = closing (toward center), -q = opening; +q on a finger = extend (+X). Self-collision is OFF, so the viewer permits closing past mesh contact; these limits are the user's visual judgement, re-verify vs CAD for exact mechanical end-stops.

servo.control: TTL half-duplex serial bus, STS-style; 12-bit (0.088 deg/pulse), 360 deg single-turn; weight 35.8 g
servo._note: Specs verified vs official FEETECH datasheet + reference/mini_gripper.xml. We actuate SLIDE joints directly, so forcerange is a LINEAR-FORCE placeholder = stall_torque / assumed pinion radius 9mm ~= 155 N (rounded to 150). Refine with CAD pinion pitch radius + verified travel, then re-tune kp/kv/damping. No-load speed is a runtime slew limit, not an MJCF field.

collision._comment: Collision geometry matches the visual meshes via CoACD convex decomposition (scripts/decompose_collision.py -> meshes/collision_pieces/), mimicking reference/pads/build_pads.py. MuJoCo collides a raw mesh as its convex hull, so the decomposition is what makes collision faithful to the non-convex visual shape. conaffinity=0 means the robot does NOT self-collide (the CAD guarantees no interference; convex-hull bloat would create false contacts) but its geoms ARE collidable with external objects/floor — same policy as the reference, which excluded every internal pair. To enable self-collision set conaffinity=1; build_mjcf then auto-excludes parent-child pairs and you can add more to exclude_pairs.
